extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners; patent examiners; Administrative Patent Judges (APJs)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for preparing and responding to appeal briefs in USPTO ex parte (and related inter partes) appeals: required brief contents, evidence appendices, examiner's answers (including new grounds), remands, oral hearings, reply briefs, and timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim patentability (no 'invention' or grouped-claims decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability must be decided on a claim-by-claim basis. Merits decisions of the Board in ex parte appeals must determine the patentability of individual claims, not whether an 'invention' is patentable or a group of claims is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments in the Appeal Brief are preferably directed to individual claims. If appellant groups claims as permitted, the Board will pick a single claim to decide the appeal as to that ground of rejection. Failure to separately argue grouped claims can constitute waiver of arguments of separate patentability (see discussion referencing In re McDaniel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver risk when grouping claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Grouping claims together for argument may waive argument that certain dependent claims are patentable for reasons independent of a representative claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The waiver provision reflects the view expressed in In re McDaniel that stating claims 'stand or fall together' can waive separate patentability arguments. If appellant wishes to preserve separate arguments, they must separately present them rather than rely on grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed format for Appeal Briefs (§ 41.37) — provide common information
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure provided for by the requirements of § 41.37 ensures that Appeal Briefs will provide the information the Board needs to render an informed decision on the issues presented for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although each appeal is unique, certain information common to each appeal is amenable to a prescribed format. Appellants should follow § 41.37(c) requirements to present explanations and arguments in a manner that permits the Board to review the record effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification: 'separate' patentability (word addition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pointing out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument for 'separate' patentability of a claim; the word 'separate' was added to § 41.37(c)(1)(vii) and § 41.67(c)(1)(vii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that merely pointing out claim recitation is distinct from asserting that a claim is separately patentable on its own merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix requirement (§ 41.37(c)(1)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: An evidence appendix must contain copies of any evidence submitted to the examiner and relied upon by the appellant in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement was aligned with § 41.7(b). If evidence was relied upon, include it in the evidence appendix; if no evidence exists, include an evidence appendix indicating 'none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status/entry of evidence in the record — rules and pre-appeal practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence submitted after final rejection is not presumed to have been entered and must be specifically admitted by the examiner as set forth in § 1.116; evidence submitted either before the first Office action or after a non-final rejection may be presumed to have been entered only when treated by an examiner in an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly, the § 41.37(c)(1)(ix) requirement of stating where in the record the evidence was entered is satisfied by (a) an explicit statement entering the evidence or (b) an Office action weighing the evidence. Prior to filing an appeal brief, if the entry status of evidence is unclear (e.g., § 1.132 declaration not mentioned in subsequent final rejection), appellants should contact the examiner to clarify, since evidence not entered cannot be relied upon in the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices when none exist (evidence & related proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 41.37(c)(ix-x) require the appeal to contain an evidence appendix and a related proceedings appendix; if no evidence or related proceedings exist, include each appendix with the indication 'none'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Table of Contents indicating that no evidence appendix or related proceedings appendix is part of the brief is acceptable to clearly indicate no evidence is being relied upon or no related decisions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents/format of an Appeal Brief (example 12-item format)
rubrics_metrics.description: An example format/content for an appeal brief with each item starting on a separate page: (1) Identification page; (2) Table of Contents; (3) Real party in interest; (4) Related appeals and interferences; (5) Status of claims; (6) Status of amendments; (7) Summary of claimed subject matter; (8) Grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal; (9) Argument; (10) Claims appendix; (11) Evidence appendix; (12) Related proceedings appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this example as a compliant format that meets the requirements published with the final rulemaking and to be incorporated into the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground of rejection in Examiner's Answer — approval & appeal conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Each examiner’s answer containing a new ground of rejection must be approved by a Technology Center Director or designee. An appeal conference is mandatory in all cases in which an acceptable appeal brief has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal conference participants should include (1) the examiner preparing the answer, (2) a supervisory patent examiner (SPE), and (3) another experienced examiner (conferee). The examiner’s answer should include 'conferees' with typed/printed names and initials; a Technology Center Director/designee must initial/approve any answer containing a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for appellant when examiner institutes a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner institutes a new ground of rejection in the examiner’s answer, the appellant has two months to either request that prosecution be reopened by filing a reply under § 1.111 or file a reply brief under § 41.41 (which would act as a request that the appeal be maintained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appellant may prefer not to reopen prosecution if the new ground is similar to a prior rejection or if the record is sufficient to address it. Reopening prosecution may prolong examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reply brief to a new ground (§ 41.39(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief filed in response to a new ground of rejection in accordance with § 41.39(b)(2) only has to address the new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a reply brief should include, each on a separate page: (1) Identification page; (2) Status of claims page(s); (3) Grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal page(s); (4) Argument page(s). Alternatively, a reply brief may be a substitute brief replacing the original brief by responding to both the new ground and all remaining grounds; in that case it must meet all § 41.37(c) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed record principle — no new amendments/evidence in reply brief absent good cause or reopening
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal should be decided upon a fixed record, not an ever-changing one. Allowing examiners to make a new ground of rejection is limited; absent a new ground, the record before the Board should remain fixed as of the date the appeal brief is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to include a new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence in a reply brief upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons were not adopted; the appellant may request that prosecution be reopened to supplement the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examiner's answer approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each supplemental examiner’s answer must be approved by a Technology Center Director or designee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the control over new grounds in primary examiner’s answers and limits open-ended supplemental answers; MPEP will provide further instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to file a reply brief — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant may file a reply brief to an examiner’s answer or a supplemental examiner’s answer within two months from the date of such examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules continue to permit the appellant to always have the last word by filing a reply brief within the two-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing — reliance limited to entered record; exceptions for new law and demonstratives
rubrics_metrics.description: At an oral hearing, the appellant may only rely on evidence that has been previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present argument that has been relied upon in the brief or reply brief, but upon a showing of good cause may rely on a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court. Demonstrative exhibits solely directed to information of record and not being relied upon to establish patentability are not precluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule was amended to permit new arguments based on recent Board or Federal Court decisions upon showing good cause and to permit demonstratives that illustrate information already of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to cancel requested oral hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may cancel a requested oral hearing if the Board decides that a hearing is not necessary (e.g., prior to hearing the Board becomes convinced the examiner’s position will be reversed or that remand is necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment was adopted to require providing appellant an opportunity to insist on a hearing in such situations; MPEP will provide examples when cancellation is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-month response period to supplemental examiner’s answer after remand (§ 41.50(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.50(a)(2) has been amended to provide a two-month period for an appellant to respond to a supplemental examiner’s answer written in response to a remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a clear time limit for action after remand and avoids earlier ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding sua sponte dismissal after supplemental answer on remand
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplemental examiner’s answer is written in response to a remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection pursuant to § 41.50(a)(1), the appellant must exercise one of two options to avoid sua sponte dismissal of the appeal as to the claims subject to the rejection for which the Board has remanded the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The options are essentially to request reopening of prosecution before the examiner or to maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief as provided in § 41.41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel discretion on disposition (remand, additional briefing, reverse/vacate, affirm); finality requires a reviewable record
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel may (1) remand to the examiner for further consideration of the rejection; (2) order the appellant to brief additionally a matter concerning the rejection; (3) reverse or vacate the rejection (with or without remand for further action); or (4) affirm the rejection. A final decision on appeal can only be reached when the record is susceptible to meaningful review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remands are often used where the record is unclear, e.g., where amendments/additional evidence were filed during appeal and it's unclear whether the examiner considered them or whether they were 'entered'. The panel has discretion to choose the best course of action in each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing (§ 41.52) — new arguments based on recent authority with good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: In a request for rehearing, the appellant may, upon a showing of good cause, rely on a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relaxes the strict limitation to previously entered evidence and arguments where a recent controlling decision justifies reopening argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes / cross-appeal briefing timing clarification (§ 41.66(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple parties are entitled to file a notice of appeal or cross-appeal, the appellant brief is due within two months from the latest filed notice of appeal or cross appeal or within two months from the expiration of the time for filing a notice of appeal or cross appeal, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment clarifies earlier ambiguity about how to compute the appellant brief due date when another party may or may not file a late notice of appeal.
